test_title: PYST 47: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 03 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The infamous Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred when Gandhi called all the Indians to observe April 6, 1919, as a day of non-violent protest against which of the following colonial policies?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rowlatt Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rowlatt Act, passed in March 1919, was officially called the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919.
 
• The act authorized the British government to imprison individuals suspected of revolutionary activities without trial for up to two years.
 
• This act sparked widespread anger and protests among Indians, as it curtailed civil liberties and judicial rights.
 
• In response, Mahatma Gandhi initiated the nationwide Satyagraha movement and called for April 6, 1919, to be observed as a day of non-violent protest.
 
• The infamous Jallianwala Bagh massacre on April 13, 1919, was a direct consequence of protests against the Rowlatt Act.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Partition of Bengal:**

 
 
• The Partition of Bengal took place in 1905 during the tenure of Lord Curzon, dividing Bengal into East Bengal and West Bengal.
 
• It was primarily justified by the British as an administrative measure but was widely seen as an attempt to divide Hindus and Muslims to weaken nationalist movements.
 
• The partition led to widespread protests and was eventually annulled in 1911.
 
 
 
• **Simon Commission:**
 
 
• The Simon Commission was a group of seven British MPs sent to India in 1928 to study constitutional reforms.
 
• It was widely opposed by Indians because it had no Indian representation, leading to protests and slogans like "Simon Go Back."
 
• Notably, Lala Lajpat Rai was injured during a protest against the Simon Commission and later succumbed to his injuries.
 
 
 
• **Minto-Morley Reforms:**
 
 
• The Minto-Morley Reforms were introduced in 1909 and aimed to provide limited political representation to Indians.
 
• It introduced separate electorates for Muslims, which sowed seeds of communalism in Indian politics.
 
• The reforms were criticized for being insufficient to meet the demands of Indian nationalists.
